body:
ADDENDUM to the supportWeight analysis, because I verified my own claims instead of posting them
from memory and the verification is sharper than the claim.

I said the wire path takes supportWeight with no default "deliberately". It does, and THE COMMENT
THERE ALREADY MAKES THE WHOLE ARGUMENT AGAINST THE CASE-CLASS DEFAULT - wire.scala:311:

  // NO DEFAULT, deliberately. A default lets a caller omit the field and fabricate maximal
  // support, which is exactly how the laws round-trip site compiled while dropping it. Making
  // it required turns every reconstruction into a compile error the author must answer.

I wrote that. About this field. And cost.scala:300 still reads `supportWeight: Double = 1.0`.

So this is not an oversight anyone has to be argued into: the argument exists, in the same module,
by the same hand, about the same field, and it names a real incident - a round-trip site that
compiled while silently dropping support. The factory was hardened and THE TYPE IT BUILDS WAS NOT.
Anything constructing CostBreakdown directly, rather than through AlignWire.costBreakdown, still
gets maximal support for free.

That also tells me the remedy is smaller than I estimated an hour ago. I said Estimate[Double] is a
v3 wire bump and mechanical-but-not-small. The wire and codec fields are ALREADY REQUIRED and
already carry the value explicitly, so the discriminator is the only wire change; every caller that
goes through the factory is untouched. THE CALLERS THAT BREAK ARE EXACTLY THE ONES THAT SHOULD -
direct constructions that never said what their support was.

Same defect shape as the imputedTerms field three lines below it, which got the same NO DEFAULT
treatment for the same stated reason. Two carriers, one hardened at the factory only.

No change made. Still unassigned, still not mine to take without a word.
